implementation_notes: asyncio.Future is the placeholder that another task or callback completes, so the requestor keeps a dict from correlation id to future, publishes, and awaits with asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout) for the deadline; the reader task looks the id up, checks the future is not done and calls set_result. pika and aio-pika expose the value as BasicProperties.correlation_id on request and reply, which is how the RabbitMQ RPC tutorial's client matches replies - the async version merely replaces the blocking receive with a future. Register the future before publishing and pop the entry in a finally block so cancellation and timeout cannot leak it.
pitfalls: asyncio.wait_for cancels the future when the deadline expires, so a late reply must not call set_result on it - check fut.done() in the reader or asyncio raises InvalidStateError in the reader task.
Calling set_result twice raises InvalidStateError: treat the pending-entry removal as the single-delivery gate and deliver before removing, under the same code path.

Futures must be created on the running loop (asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()); the deprecated loop= parameter and get_event_loop() outside a coroutine produce futures bound to the wrong loop.
A future that is never resolved keeps its awaiting task suspended, so every timeout and cancellation path must remove the entry or both the dict and the suspending coroutine leak.

variants.name: concurrent.futures table with a reader thread (synchronous stacks)
variants.implementation_notes: In synchronous stacks - pika's BlockingConnection, plain sockets, CLI RPC clients - the same table holds concurrent.futures.Future objects and a dedicated reader thread completes them while the caller blocks in fut.result(timeout=...), which raises concurrent.futures.TimeoutError on expiry. This is the shape of the RabbitMQ RPC tutorial's client, including its discipline of comparing the reply's correlation_id against the outstanding request and discarding unknown ids instead of failing. Choose it when there is no event loop; inside an async application the asyncio variant is preferable because it avoids the extra thread and the lock.
pitfalls: concurrent.futures.Future.set_result raises InvalidStateError when the future is already done, and a late reply arriving after the caller timed out must be dropped rather than delivered - guard with done() under the lock.
The reader thread must not die on one bad message: wrap per-message handling so a single malformed or uncorrelated reply cannot silently stop the only delivery path.
fut.result(timeout=...) only stops waiting; the request is still outstanding, so keep the id reserved until it is purged or a late reply can satisfy the next request.
TimeoutError here is concurrent.futures.TimeoutError (aliased to the builtin only since Python 3.11), so catch the right class when targeting older interpreters.
